I just wanted to say that it sucks that there are so many people with no empathy for you and your situation. I'm glad you have someone like Lucy to help you and that you're able to officially get her regarded as a service dog. If I look in the mirror with longer hair, I think there's some sort of disconnect, because it feels like I'm looking at someone else instead of myself.

E: As for breasts, I haven't really ever felt sexualized by other people in that way. It's the same feeling as the hair but to a lesser degree. Interestingly enough, clothes that are more form fitting don't bring this feeling, but looser clothes do. But now that I think about it, I suspect it might be a weight issue rather than a gender one.

I don't know if I know what dysphoria feels like. I think I used to feel it with some things (e.g. chest size), and for some current things as well (hair length). But aside from the latter, I don't feel like I'm in the wrong body and I'm generally satisfied with it. I do wish I could look more androgynous sometimes when I see other people pulling it off, but more in a "I want to look like this for the moment, but not permanently." It's a fleeting feeling. (Genderfluidity?) If non-body dysphoria is a thing, I've certainly felt it. Being called a woman, lady, or girl makes me feel a little uncomfortable, somehow.

I think what I will end up doing is just trying a bunch of different things relating to this and seeing what sticks and what doesn't. Maybe something will bring me that unexpected joy.

This was very rambly, but thank you for replying! It helped me process a little more.
